cards.subject: Durnholde Keep
lines: Aedelas Blackmoore ran the orc internment camps from this fortress, and raised, trained and beat Thrall inside it as a gladiator.
Thrall came back, killed him in single combat, and called on the earth to level the place. The rubble is the aftermath of the boy coming home.

cards.subject: Southshore is a town
cards.tag: Nothing has happened to it yet
lines: Inn, stables, forge, mailbox, flight master, a magistrate, a graveyard. No bank, no auction house.
The blight, the ruins and the refugees everyone remembers are Cataclysm.
Here it is a place where people are brewing beer.

cards.subject: What Southshore sells
lines: Chef Jessen is renowned for his Soothing Turtle Bisque, and the turtles are off the strand below the town.
They brew Sparkling Southshore Cider and Southshore Stout.
Bartolo Ginsetti sells famous Yeti Fur Cloaks, made from the things in the caves up the hill.

cards.subject: Tarren Mill
lines: A church, a few houses, withered orchards. The Forsaken hold it now, apothecaries and all.
But it has not been rebuilt into a Forsaken town yet — that redesign is Cataclysm.
They are living inside somebody else's village and the church is still standing.

cards.subject: Tarren Mill and Southshore
lines: Two towns, one road, a few minutes apart, and no battleground yet invented to drain the pressure off.
It escalated from duels to twenty and thirty-player raids until the servers buckled — five second latency was common.
The nicknames are what the zone got called for it.

cards.subject: Taretha Foxton
cards.tag: At the keep you are standing in
lines: The human girl who fed the infant Thrall, wrote to him in his cell, and covered his escape.
Blackmoore executed her and threw her head at him from the battlements.
It was the first time Thrall wept. There is no marker here for her.

cards.subject: Zul'jin was in there
lines: Before the ruins, the keep held the Amani forest troll warlord. Orgrim Doomhammer personally led the raid that broke him out.
That was the price the Amani set for guiding the Horde north.
It is why the Horde marched on Quel'Thalas instead of straight at Lordaeron.

cards.subject: The Lion of Azeroth
lines: The first major land battle of the Second War was fought on this ground. Doomhammer landed unopposed near Southshore.
Death knights raised the Alliance's own dead against them until Uther's paladins steadied the line.
Nothing here marks it. You are just walking through fields.

cards.subject: Dun Garok
cards.tag: A dwarf keep in a human zone
lines: Ironforge mountaineers, riflemen and priests garrisoned in the southeastern hills, there to shield Hillsbrad's people and the Azurelode Mine.
The Forsaken loathed having them there and paid adventurers to go in and kill every one.

cards.subject: Everything wants the water
lines: Daggerspine naga hold the shore, Torn Fin murlocs work the Eastern Strand and prey on passing ships, and the yetis are in the caves inland.
Southshore keeps a privateer fleet whose stated job is keeping the waterways clear.
It is not winning.

cards.subject: Purgation Isle
lines: The spiral of rock in the water is haunted by dozens of condemned human and dwarf spirits — paladins, priests, monks and mages, bound into service by an ogre necromancer.
Before the First War the island belonged to Kul Tiras.
After Cataclysm the ghosts are gone. This is the only version with them on it.

cards.subject: Helcular's grave
lines: A Horde chain has you charge a dead wizard's rod at three flames, then drive it into a grave inside Southshore.
He gets up: a level forty-four elite who walks the churchyard raising skeletons for about ten minutes, and then fades.
Deleted from the game in 4.0.3a.

cards.subject: Why he is buried there
lines: "Master Helcular was almost complete with his transformation into a Lich when a human lynch mob discovered his ritual lair in the hills and brutally killed him."
Southshore's own townsfolk killed him and then buried him in their churchyard.
His apprentice wants the rains of vengeance to fall on the town. That is why the grave is the target.
